acceptance: CLI help for --capture-plans and --analyze-plans/--no-analyze-plans, feature docs, CLI reference and Python API docs all state: estimated EXPLAIN by default; --analyze-plans opts into post-measurement ANALYZE where the engine supports it.
An executable test drives the real run CLI for omitted flag, --analyze-plans and --no-analyze-plans on DuckDB and asserts per-operator timing presence matches the documented contract.

Docs distinguish capture opt-in, deferred-phase eligibility and actual adapter/parser capability, and say a matching fingerprint means matching normalized logical structure, not identical physical plans; remove the unsupported DuckDB estimate exception.

Docs describe the SQL vs DataFrame result fields as implemented after DataFrame parity and the limits of post-measurement EXPLAIN for bespoke mid-run mutations; make docs-check/compat checks pass and add a changelog.d fragment.
context: Merged via PR #3709 as cf08807f9 on develop. CI and oracle review passed on the merged head. Public docs merged in BenchBox-dev/benchbox-site#84 as fd4e85961. Decision recorded: estimated EXPLAIN stays the default (qpc-04); help and docs corrected.
description: CLI help and query-plan-analysis.md promise ANALYZE capture by default, but PlatformAdapter defaults analyze_plans to false and a real CLI run without either analyze flag captured estimated plans with null operator timing. Decision (recorded during review): keep the estimated default. qpc-04 (#1016, 2026-07-06) is the latest code decision and deliberately chose estimated EXPLAIN with an ANALYZE opt-in notice; the doc prose claiming ANALYZE default dates from 2026-06-24 (#887) and was never reconciled. So fix help/docs, not code. Other contract drift to fix: phase eligibility described as capability, a DuckDB estimate-fingerprint exception the structural signature does not support, and generic result-field claims that do not hold for DataFrame results (update after DataFrame parity lands).
